title: Zanzibar island system
framing: Zanzibar is not one beach. Stone Town, the north, north-east, east/south-east and south-west each produce different combinations of history, swimming, tides, reefs, nightlife, quiet and onward travel.

reference_facts.island_note: The main island of Unguja combines a UNESCO-listed historic city, reef-fringed coasts, tidal flats, fishing villages, resorts and agricultural landscapes.
reference_facts.tide_note: Tidal range strongly affects many east and south-east beaches; northern beaches such as Nungwi/Kendwa are generally less disrupted for swimming.
reference_facts.season_note: June–October is generally drier/cooler; January–February is hotter and relatively dry; the long rains are typically concentrated around March–May with shorter rains often around November.
reference_facts.heritage_note: Stone Town's urban fabric reflects long African, Arab, Indian and European interaction through Indian Ocean trade.

zones.name: Stone Town & west
zones.strongest_use: 1–2 nights before or after the beach
zones.summary: Historic streets, seafront, markets, architecture and food create a completely different Zanzibar from the beach resorts.
zones.swimming: Not the island's strongest beach base; the value is urban and cultural.
zones.tides: Tides matter less to the experience than on the east coast.
zones.atmosphere: Dense, walkable, social and historically layered.
zones.tradeoff: Heat, traffic and urban intensity make it a poor substitute for beach recovery.

zones.name: North · Nungwi / Kendwa
zones.summary: Northern beaches are among the easiest places on the island for swimming through more of the tidal cycle, with stronger resort and nightlife infrastructure.
zones.swimming: One of the island's strongest swimming areas.
zones.tides: Less disruptive than many east-coast beaches, though tides still exist.
zones.atmosphere: More social, busier and more developed.
zones.tradeoff: Less quiet and less village-scale than many east/south-east locations.

zones.name: North-east · Matemwe / Mnemba-facing coast
zones.strongest_use: Diving, snorkeling and quieter beach time
zones.summary: The north-east combines long beaches with access toward the Mnemba reef system and a generally quieter atmosphere than Nungwi.
zones.swimming: Good in suitable tidal windows, but more tide-dependent than the north.
zones.tides: Meaningful; daily timing affects beach and water use.
zones.tradeoff: Travellers wanting all-day easy swimming may prefer the north.

zones.name: East & south-east · Paje / Jambiani / Bwejuu
zones.strongest_use: Long beach days, kitesurfing, slower stays
zones.summary: Broad pale beaches and dramatic tidal movement define much of the east and south-east coast.
zones.swimming: Excellent at the right tide, but shallow reef flats can make low tide a completely different experience.
zones.tides: A central part of the day rather than a minor detail.
zones.atmosphere: Long, open, active and increasingly social around Paje; quieter farther south or in smaller villages.
zones.tradeoff: Not ideal for travellers expecting deep-water swimming directly in front of the hotel all day.

zones.name: South & south-west
zones.strongest_use: Slow stays away from the busiest resort zones
zones.summary: Southern and south-western areas offer quieter coastal rhythms, mangrove/lagoon environments in places, fishing communities and west-facing sunset possibilities.
zones.swimming: Highly location-specific; some areas are less straightforward for classic beach swimming.
zones.tides: Can be significant depending on the exact bay or shoreline.
zones.tradeoff: Less convenient for travellers prioritising resort variety or guaranteed easy swimming.

seasonal_calendar.planning_note: Strong for beach and diving, but heat and humidity are more pronounced.

seasonal_calendar.climate: Long-rains period with heavier showers and more unsettled conditions.
seasonal_calendar.planning_note: Some properties or marine operators may reduce operations or close; confirm actual availability.
One of the easiest periods to combine with mainland dry-season safari.

seasonal_calendar.climate: Warm, generally dry and increasingly hot toward October.
seasonal_calendar.planning_note: Strong all-round coast period; marine conditions still vary by day and coast.

seasonal_calendar.climate: Short-rain period can bring intermittent showers.
seasonal_calendar.planning_note: Often still highly usable for beach travel, but weather is less predictable.

seasonal_calendar.climate: Warmer festive-season conditions with mixed but often improving weather.
seasonal_calendar.planning_note: High-demand period; accommodation availability and pricing become major planning factors.

stay_logic.note: Enough for either Stone Town or beach, but not both without rushing.
Works for a single beach base after safari or a short Stone Town + beach split.
The strongest general default for safari recovery plus one layer of island context.
Makes two coastal contexts, diving, slower beach rhythm or Stone Town + beach feel deliberate rather than appended.

activities.name: Swimming
activities.note: Best matched by coast; north is generally easier for all-day swimming, while east/south-east is more tide-led.

activities.name: Diving / snorkeling
activities.note: Strong around reef systems, but visibility, sea state, certification and operator quality matter.

activities.name: Kitesurfing
activities.note: Especially associated with east/south-east areas such as Paje; wind conditions vary seasonally.

activities.name: Stone Town
activities.note: Best treated as its own urban chapter rather than a half-day excursion from a distant beach.

activities.name: Spice / food / village context
activities.note: Useful when locally guided and specific; avoid turning the island into a checklist of staged stops.

traveller_fit.note: Works best when the coast is designed around the traveller's energy after safari rather than automatically adding activities.
Strongest when the exact coast is chosen around swimming, quiet, food and privacy rather than generic luxury.
Swimming conditions, room setup, transfers and activity age limits matter more than island-level labels.
Choose coast and property around actual marine access rather than beach appearance alone.
The island becomes much richer when Stone Town and Swahili/Indian Ocean history are treated as central rather than optional.

route_shapes.label: Stone Town + north
route_shapes.note: A strong first-island shape when travellers want both urban context and straightforward swimming.

route_shapes.label: Stone Town + east/south-east
route_shapes.note: Best when the traveller understands and welcomes tidal beach rhythm.

route_shapes.label: Safari → beach only
best_for: travellers who already know Stone Town
route_shapes.note: Valid when rest is the priority; Stone Town should not be forced into every trip.

operated_evidence.label: Operated · couple
operated_evidence.title: History before the beach
operated_evidence.insight: The couple began Zanzibar in Stone Town, then moved north to Nungwi so the final days could become deliberately quieter and easier to swim.

publication_rules: Do not describe all Zanzibar beaches as equivalent.
Do not guarantee all-day swimming outside specific coast/property context.
Treat tides as a practical planning factor, especially on the east and south-east coast.
Do not guarantee marine visibility, dolphin encounters or specific reef wildlife.
Do not hard-code marine-transfer times or seasonal operator availability.
Keep Stone Town heritage distinct from generic 'spice island' marketing.
